meeting_header: Date: 2025-04-01 | Time: 15:00-15:42 UTC | Duration: 42 minutes | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Nguyen (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Sailwave - ML Lead), Raj Patel (Sailwave - Eng Manager), Sophie Green (Sailwave - Product)
summary: Weekly POC check-in to review quality eval results. Discussed recent regression on intent classification prompts after moving to the quantized model, prompt set tweaks, scoring thresholds, and guardrails. Agreed on specific re-runs and deliverables: Redwood to share security docs, re-run quantized eval for per-prompt breakdown, customer to share failing cases. Plan a deeper Dedicated vs Private deployment call next week.
topics: Quality regressions observed on 3 prompt clusters
Deployment options impact (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
transcript: 00:00 Maya: OK, uh, thanks everyone for joining, quick roll call — Maya Patel here from Redwood. 00:06 Carlos: Carlos Nguyen, SE on the POC. 00:09 Laura: Laura Chen, ML lead at Sailwave. 00:12 Raj: Raj Patel, engineering. 00:14 Sophie: Sophie Green, product. 00:17 Maya: Cool, quick agenda — quality results from last week's run, regression points, prompt fixes, and next steps. We have about 42 minutes so we'll cover the top issues. 01:05 Carlos: Alright jumping in, I pulled the per-prompt scoring spreadsheet — note I also attached the run id to the shared drive, link in chat — but highlights: overall aggregate accuracy held around 87% for the float32 model but dropped to 81% on the 8-bit quantized variant. 01:28 Laura: Yea that's consistent with what we saw locally, the intent classification slip is the pain point. 01:40 Raj: Just to clarify, are you using the same prompt templates or did the prompt tuning change between runs? 01:46 Carlos: Same canonical prompt set but there was a small change: we normalized punctuation in the float run but a preprocessor mismatch happened for the quant run — some prompts lacked trailing question marks, so the model context weighting shifted. 02:12 Sophie: Hm, so maybe it's a preproc bug rather than pure model quality. 02:20 Carlos: Partly. We also saw two clusters where hallucination increased — the ones with multi-step user intent and ambiguous entity references. 03:05 Maya: Can you give a quick example of a failing prompt? — not exact PII but sanitized. 03:12 Laura: Sure, example A: "How do I migrate my data from old fleet to new instance?" expected intent: migration -> route to migration flow; model returned a generic troubleshooting piece which then caused downstream routing to the wrong flow. 03:36 Carlos: In the spreadsheet that example's score dropped from 0.92 to 0.57, so big regression. 04:10 Sophie: Are we scoring by annotation match or using similarity thresholds? 04:18 Carlos: We're using a combined metric: token-level similarity and intent slot match; it's a custom scoring script — quick note: we may need to tighten thresholds for the quant run. 05:00 Raj: Any timing/latency differences between float and quant that could affect production choice? 05:06 Carlos: Latency is slightly better on quant, average per-request latency down ~10-15% in our test harness, cost reduced ~18% per-token. But tradeoff is the quality delta on those edge prompt clusters. 05:42 Laura: For us the routing mistake is high-severity — it converts to wrong UX and support churn. So cost savings are less interesting if we lose those critical intents. 06:15 Maya: Understood — that's why guardrails matter. We can add an intent confidence threshold that triggers fallback to the float model or a verification step. 06:35 Carlos: Exactly — we can do smart routing by confidence. For low-confidence prompts, route to float32 hosted or to Dedicated depending on SLA. 07:02 Raj: How feasible is that in the POC timeline? 07:08 Carlos: We can wire up a confidence-based route in the POC by next week, it's mostly config and a small check in the inference path. 07:22 Sophie: Can we also add a forced clarification prompt when confidence is low instead of immediate fallback? 07:28 Maya: Yes, we can do clarification flows as a quick mitigation. 08:05 Laura: On the scoring side, we want per-prompt breakdowns and anonymized examples. 08:12 Carlos: Agreed — I'll re-run the batch and include per-prompt deltas and raw model outputs. 08:40 Maya: Also, we noted some guardrail hits — hallucination filters and unsafe content detectors triggered on a few examples unexpectedly. 08:52 Laura: Those were in the multi-step prompts? 08:59 Carlos: Yeah, the detector was tripped when the model invented a vendor name; not harmful but flagged. Might be sensitivity tuning. 09:30 Raj: Any compliance concerns? We need to see logs, encryption in transit + at rest, and KMS usage. 09:40 Maya: We'll attach the SOC2 summary and a KMS architecture diagram after this call. 09:50 Sophie: For deployment we also need to know about VPC options — how much of the control plane is customer-managed in the Private offering? 10:00 Maya: Private gives you a customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem. We'll schedule a deeper dive with the infra team next week. 10:18 Laura: Back to prompts — we have 3 clusters that produce most failures: migration intents, billing edge cases, and multi-entity disambiguation. 10:35 Carlos: If we canonicalize and add extra instruction tokens to the prompt for those clusters we can often recover most of the quality. 11:02 Raj: What's the expected lift from canonicalization? 11:06 Carlos: Based on prior runs, adding explicit slot instructions and examples lifts those clusters by 6-10 points in our scoring. 11:22 Sophie: Any risk of overfitting to the prompt set? We don't want brittle prompts. 11:30 Maya: Right, we recommend a mix: keep canonicalization plus small paraphrase augmentation to avoid brittleness. 12:10 Laura: For the failing examples we'll include counterexamples and expected outputs — that'll help tune thresholds. 12:25 Carlos: Also will run bracketed tests with temperature changes; quantized models sometimes respond better to lower temps. 13:00 Raj: Are there feature flags to toggle the quant model in production for small percentages? 13:07 Maya: Yes, Redwood Dedicated supports canary rollouts with percent traffic and automatic fallback policies. 13:20 Sophie: Great — we could canary 5% first with guardrails. 14:02 Carlos: Quick note on metrics: we'll include per-prompt precision/recall for slot extraction and an intent confusion matrix. 14:20 Laura: That confusion matrix will be helpful to see which intents are getting swapped. 15:10 Maya: Any legal or procurement blockers on the horizon? 15:15 Raj: We're still reviewing the MSA; expect comments from legal next week. 15:22 Maya: Cool, AE will follow up on procurement timeline. 16:00 Sophie: One other data residency question — some customers require EU-only logs; can Redwood restrict logs by region in Private? 16:10 Maya: In Private yes, in Dedicated we can configure region affinity and retention — I'll get specific retention SLA language to you. 16:48 Carlos: Back to the regression — I'll prioritize re-running the quantized eval with the exact preproc fixes to isolate the effect. 17:05 Laura: If preproc fixes recover the score then we're good to use quant, otherwise we need routing by confidence for those clusters. 17:30 Maya: Ok decision tree noted: try preproc + prompt tweaks; if <3 point recovery then enable confidence routing + clarification flow. 18:05 Raj: For the re-run, what's the expected time to get results? 18:10 Carlos: I can run overnight and share results by 2025-04-04. 19:02 Sophie: Can you also share sample logs to prove no sensitive fields leaking? 19:10 Maya: We'll sanitize and provide sample audit logs and the masking policy. 20:00 Laura: A couple of smaller UX asks: add a per-request token count in the logs and a cost estimate for the canary. 20:12 Carlos: We'll include token counts and cost delta estimates for the canary. 21:35 Maya: Alright wrapping up — recap of next steps: Carlos rerun, Maya send security docs + schedule deep-dive, Laura share failing examples. Anything else? 21:50 Raj: Legal timeline note — expect MSA comments by next Tue. 22:05 Sophie: We'll be ready to approve a 5% canary after the re-run results. 22:30 Maya: Great, thanks everyone. We'll sync next week same time. 22:40 (call ends)
